shared_elements: upright rectangular pillar/slab as the carved surface
low-relief animal in profile (quadruped) on the pillar face
rows of small repeated units (pitted cupmarks in A / row of repeated arched motifs in B)
plain undecorated ground around the carved motifs
justification: Both show a faint low-relief animal in profile placed on the upper face of a tall plain upright slab, plus rows of small repeated units (cupmarks in A, repeated arch motifs in B), which is a real if modest correspondence in motif type and relief convention. The decisive difference is density and content: B carries a full multi-register programme of quadrupeds, a bird, a snake and a woven/net band stacked in order, while A's surfaces are almost entirely blank architectural stone with one isolated animal sign and a pitted block, and no comparable combinations or relationships between figures.
